# mxroute_reseller_user (Resource)

Manage a reseller-owned user through a **plain reseller** provider (not an impersonation alias). Creation and explicit rotation require a write-only password of at least 8 characters and a positive rotation version; server strength rules still apply and import requires no password. Updates run in a fixed order — unsuspend, package reassignment, password/quota PATCH, suspend — and record each confirmed step so a failed later step is retried alone. Delete permanently removes the user account and everything it hosts. Runtime behavior is live-unverified.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "customer_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

# Use a plain reseller provider, not a reseller|user impersonation alias.
resource "mxroute_reseller_user" "customer" {
  username            = "customer1"
  email               = "owner@example.net" # changing it REPLACES the user
  package             = mxroute_reseller_package.starter.name
  quota_mb            = "2048" # MB, or "unlimited"; omit to adopt the package value
  suspended           = false
  password_wo         = var.customer_password
  password_wo_version = 1 # increase to rotate

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true # deletion removes the account and everything it hosts
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) Contact email used at creation. No update route is documented, so changing it plans a REPLACEMENT that deletes the user and its data; protect important users with `prevent_destroy`. Remote changes appear in `current_email` and never trigger replacement. Import adopts the remote value.
- `package` (String) Assigned package. Changes are applied in place through the package-assignment endpoint. Reference `mxroute_reseller_package.<name>.name` so users are removed before their packages.
- `username` (String) Username. New users require 1–10 lowercase letters, digits or underscores; imported users may use the 1–16 character authentication syntax. Compared exactly. Changing it REPLACES the user.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only password, required on creation and when password_wo_version increases. Read from configuration only; never persisted in plan or state. Omit on updates to preserve the remote credential. Imports do not require a password.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Positive rotation version. Required with password_wo. Increase to rotate; retain the existing version when omitting the password. Imported objects may omit both fields until their first explicit rotation.
- `quota_mb` (String) Effective user disk quota in **MB**, or `unlimited` (package quota is GB). When set, it is an explicit override applied after any package reassignment and re-applied if reassignment changed it. Omission adopts the server value and never sends a quota. Package/override precedence is live-unverified.
- `suspended` (Boolean) Suspension state. Changes dispatch suspend or unsuspend only when the remote state differs. Omission adopts the server value.

### Read-Only

- `current_email` (String) Server-reported contact email.
- `domain` (String) Server-reported primary domain.
- `id` (String) Username; account-relative to the plain reseller provider.
- `quota_used_mb` (Number) Volatile disk usage in MB.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import mxroute_reseller_user.customer customer1
```
